- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +10–15% above peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a dip, model may lag; forecast should align with sentiment shift within 2–3 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >15% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10%.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction; match forecast to sentiment polarity.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >5% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with that trend.
